metric: Debian popcon sourcemax installations by source package (pinned snapshot)
note: Leads are not verified parsers. Ranks are assigned only among verified paths.

leads.name: libreoffice
leads.reason: Office suite. Its SQL parser (connectivity/source/parse, OSQLParser) is internal to LibreOffice Base and is not part of the LibreOffice SDK or any Debian development package, so there is no documented library API to call on local SQL text.

leads.name: gdal
leads.reason: GDAL's OGR SQL dialect parser (swq_select in ogr_swq.h) backs GDALDataset::ExecuteSQL over vector datasets. The documented OGR SQL dialect supports SELECT and a few DDL statements but not INSERT, so the second valid control cannot be parsed, and swq_select is not a documented public parsing API. The popcon count covers the whole geospatial library.

leads.name: antlr4-cpp-runtime
leads.reason: ANTLR 4 C++ runtime only; it ships no SQL grammar or generated SQL parser.

leads.name: sqlitebrowser
leads.family: DB Browser for SQLite internal SQLite schema parser
leads.reason: Desktop application (DB Browser for SQLite). Its SQL parsing is internal to the application and is not shipped as a library or development package.

leads.name: soci
leads.reason: Database access wrapper; sends SQL to a backend and has no SQL parser.

leads.name: kdb
leads.reason: KDb (Kexi database library). KDbParser parses KDb SQL into a KDbQuerySchema, but it requires a KDbConnection to resolve tables and its grammar covers SELECT only, so it cannot parse the INSERT control without a database connection.

leads.name: mysql++
leads.reason: MySQL client wrapper; no SQL parser.

leads.name: libvsqlitepp
leads.reason: SQLite C++ wrapper; uses sqlite3_prepare and has no syntax tree.

leads.name: sqlitestudio
leads.reason: Desktop application. Its SQLite parser lives in the application's coreSQLiteStudio library, which Debian does not ship as a development package with a documented API.

leads.name: libpg-query
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: C library; recorded in the C cell. No C++ binding package in Debian.

leads.name: duckdb
leads.family: DuckDB PEG parser (own grammar and transformer)
leads.reason: DuckDB engine (Debian source duckdb). duckdb::Parser::GetBuiltinParser().ParseQuery parses both valid controls without a database or client context into SQLStatement trees that give the oracle summary (COUNT(*) is stored as count_star and reported as count). v2.0.0 replaced the libpg_query-derived bison grammar of DuckDB 1.x with its own PEG grammar, so it is no longer in the PostgreSQL grammar family.

leads.name: libodb
leads.reason: ODB object-relational mapper runtime; generates SQL, no parser.

leads.name: hsql (hyrise/sql-parser)
leads.metric_error: no Debian source package; no Homebrew formula
leads.reason: hsql::SQLParser::parse returns SQLParserResult with SQLStatement trees; documented local text API. No Debian source package in the pinned popcon snapshot (rechecked 2026-11-17 for hsql, hyrise and sql-parser source names), so it has no value for this cell's primary popcon metric and no Debian dev-package fallback; GitHub stars are not allowed outside PLY cells.

leads.name: qgis
leads.reason: Round 3 targeted lookup. QGIS core's QgsSQLStatement parses SELECT statements for OGC filter translation, but its grammar (src/core/qgssqlstatementparser.yy at tag final-3_40_0) declares SELECT, JOIN, WHERE and ORDER BY and has no GROUP BY or INSERT, so it cannot parse either control. The popcon count is for the whole QGIS application. Debian popcon sourcemax rank 5,103, 1,927 installations (pinned snapshot).

leads.name: futuresql
leads.reason: Round 3 targeted lookup. Asynchronous Qt database access library (QtSql drivers underneath); it passes statement text to the database driver and has no SQL parser. Debian popcon sourcemax rank 1,911, 24,225 installations (pinned snapshot).
